---
title: "Readings — Crosslinking and fixation"
---

Reading is optional, but each item is here for a reason. Start with the two marked **start
here** if you read nothing else: one covers the chemistry of the reversible case, the other
the chemistry of the irreversible one.

## Formaldehyde: what the bond is

**Hoffman EA, Frey BL, Smith LM, Auble DT (2015).** *Formaldehyde crosslinking: a tool for the
study of chromatin complexes.* Journal of Biological Chemistry 290:26404–26411.
[doi:10.1074/jbc.R115.651679](https://doi.org/10.1074/jbc.R115.651679) — **start here**

> The methylol adduct, the methylene bridge, which groups react and how reversal works. Read
> it for the two-step mechanism and for how little of the chemistry inside a cell is actually
> measured.

**Solomon MJ, Varshavsky A (1985).** *Formaldehyde-mediated DNA–protein crosslinking: a probe
for in vivo chromatin structures.* PNAS 82:6470–6474.
[doi:10.1073/pnas.82.19.6470](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.82.19.6470)

> The paper that turned fixation into a mapping method, and the ancestor of every ChIP. Look
> at what they had to show before the crosslink could be trusted as a report of contact.

**Jackson V (1978).** *Studies on histone organization in the nucleosome using formaldehyde as a
reversible cross-linking agent.* Cell 15:945–954.
[doi:10.1016/0092-8674(78)90278-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0092-8674(78)90278-7)

> Earlier, and worth a look for the word *reversible* in the title: the reversal was the point
> from the beginning.

## Dose, time and what goes wrong

**Schmiedeberg L, Skene P, Deaton A, Bird A (2009).** *A temporal threshold for formaldehyde
crosslinking and fixation.* PLoS ONE 4:e4636.
[doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0004636](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0004636)

> How long fixation takes to immobilise a protein, measured rather than assumed. Useful for
> seeing why short fixations behave differently from long ones.

**Baranello L, Kouzine F, Sanford S, Levens D (2016).** *ChIP bias as a function of
cross-linking time.* Chromosome Research 24:175–181.
[doi:10.1007/s10577-015-9509-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10577-015-9509-1)

> The same chromatin fixed for different times gives different maps. Read it before you treat
> a fixation time copied from another laboratory as a neutral choice.

**Gavrilov AA, Razin SV, Cavalli G (2015).** *In vivo formaldehyde cross-linking: it is time for
black box analysis.* Briefings in Functional Genomics 14:163–165.
[doi:10.1093/bfgp/elu037](https://doi.org/10.1093/bfgp/elu037)

> Short, and a useful corrective: what is known about crosslinking efficiency in a cell, and
> what is assumed.

## Longer arms, and the UV case

**Zeng PY, Vakoc CR, Chen ZC, Blobel GA, Berger SL (2006).** *In vivo dual cross-linking for
identification of indirect DNA-associated proteins by chromatin immunoprecipitation.*
BioTechniques 41:694–698. [doi:10.2144/000112297](https://doi.org/10.2144/000112297)

> The two-reagent protocol, and the argument for it: which targets are invisible to
> formaldehyde alone.

**Lee FCY, Ule J (2018).** *Advances in CLIP technologies for studies of protein–RNA
interactions.* Molecular Cell 69:354–369.
[doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2018.01.005](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molcel.2018.01.005) —
**start here**

> The UV side in one review. Read the sections on crosslinking efficiency and on what the
> peptide stub does to reverse transcription; the rest is the method family, which belongs to
> the RNA modifications deck.

**Alles J, Karaiskos N, Praktiknjo SD, et al. (2017).** *Cell fixation and preservation for
droplet-based single-cell transcriptomics.* BMC Biology 15:44.
[doi:10.1186/s12915-017-0383-5](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12915-017-0383-5)

> Fixation treated as a sample-handling problem rather than a chemistry problem. Compare what
> methanol and formaldehyde do to the same cells.

## Reference material to keep open

- **A crosslinker selection guide** from any supplier of bifunctional reagents. The table is
  the same four columns as the lecture figure — reactive group, spacer-arm length, membrane
  permeability, cleavability — and reading one is the skill, not memorising a reagent.
- **[NGS 101](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/)** pages for
  [ChIP-seq](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/chip-seq__10.1038+nmeth1068/chip-seq.html),
  [iCLIP](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/iclip__10.1038+nsmb.1838/iclip_partial.html)
  and [Micro-C](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/micro-c__10.1016+j.cell.2015.05.048/micro-c.html)
  give the fixation conditions, the reversal conditions and where each sits in the protocol.
